findings: The decide-economics fix worked as designed: 16/15 decisions landed (up from 5/0 in w52) with the 90s timeout + the 45s pacer — no more total starvation.

The ceiling is real: two agents' concurrent ~2200-token prefills exceed even the 90s budget on the iGPU (the throughput splits across slots). Some decides still timed out (5 tick failures, one startup PlayingBackendError).
own_pos stayed 0 — without reliably-served decides the agents never reached the actuation cadence.
the_decisive_next_move: Serve Clef from HEAVENGRAPH (2x RTX 8000 48GB, criterion 6's third benchmark leg): the 9B Q4 at CUDA speeds decides in well under a second, ends every flavor of decide-latency flakiness permanently, and the agents point at heavengraph over the LAN. Deployment: the CUDA llama.cpp build there (spike 006 pattern), the model file staged, the decide-url pointed at it; the ROCm local box stays the fallback.
also_valid_tonight: The 90s timeout + the 45s pacer stay (correct for ANY backend); the prompt could also be trimmed (~2200 tokens is mostly the state JSON) as a secondary lever.
